summary: PWA service-worker regression check passed. index.js guarded controllerchange auto-reload + sw.js CACHE_NAME v3 did not break the app. Login page renders, SW registers (no failure), no reload loop before/after login/refresh, wrong password shows specific 'Invalid email or password' via data-testid=login-error, admin login lands on /, session persists after reload.

test_results.sw_registered_console_log: PASS - '[PWA] Service Worker registered' seen, no registration failed error
test_results.no_reload_loop: PASS - main-frame nav count stayed low (4 total across full flow incl. login redirect + manual refresh)
test_results.session_persists_on_refresh: PASS - stayed on / after reload, no bounce to /login, no post-refresh reload loop

critical_code_review_comments: index.js controllerchange listener is properly guarded (only attached when navigator.serviceWorker.controller exists, and uses a 'refreshing' latch) — safe against reload loops.
sw.js correctly bumps CACHE_NAME to rebel-trade-v3 and deletes old caches on activate; skipWaiting + clients.claim will surface new builds on next load as intended.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Preview is same-origin so the original 'stale installed PWA' bug cannot be reproduced here — only regression coverage. In this environment the first SW install did not trigger a controllerchange reload (controller was null on first load, as designed). To force a real-world upgrade test you'd need to install the PWA, then deploy a change to sw.js and reopen the installed app.
